title: delivery listing is not scoped to the caller's organization
what_is_wrong: The query filters only on endpoint_id taken from the URL path, so any authenticated user can read the delivery rows of any other organization's endpoint by guessing an integer id.

title: scheme check accepts plain http and any scheme that merely starts with "http"
what_is_wrong: `parsed.scheme.startswith("http")` passes `http://`, `httpx://` and `httpfoo://`, so non-TLS and bogus schemes are stored as delivery targets.

title: no host validation on a URL the server will later fetch
what_is_wrong: The route stores any netloc the user supplies, including `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `169.254.169.254`, and the worker then POSTs signed internal requests to it.

title: limit query parameter has a lower bound but no upper bound
what_is_wrong: `Query(50, ge=1)` lets a caller pass `limit=100000000`, so a single request can pull an unbounded number of rows including their full JSONB payloads.

title: 201 body is built from a flushed-but-uncommitted row
what_is_wrong: `to_dict()` is returned inside the `with session_scope()` block after only `flush()`, so a failure at commit time still hands the client a 201 with an id and secret for a row that was rolled back.

title: url and event_types are unvalidated free-form strings
what_is_wrong: `url: str` and `event_types: list[str]` carry no length bound, format, or membership check, so arbitrarily long strings and unknown event names are persisted.

title: no cap on endpoints per organization
what_is_wrong: Nothing limits how many endpoints one org can register, so a loop of POSTs multiplies every future event into unbounded delivery rows and outbound requests.

title: endpoint listing has no pagination
what_is_wrong: The handler calls `.all()` over every endpoint of the org with no limit or ordering, so response size grows without bound.

title: webhook enqueue happens in a transaction separate from the event insert
what_is_wrong: The event row is committed when `session_scope()` exits and only afterwards is `enqueue_for_event` awaited, so a crash in between leaves a persisted event with no delivery rows and no outbox to recover it.

title: enqueue failure is swallowed as a warning and the event reports success
what_is_wrong: Any exception from `enqueue_for_event` is caught, logged at WARNING, and `dispatch` returns the event id, so webhook deliveries are dropped silently with no retry or failure signal to the caller.

title: a hardcoded allowlist silently overrides per-endpoint subscriptions
what_is_wrong: Only the three literal types in `WEBHOOK_EVENT_TYPES` ever reach `enqueue_for_event`, so an endpoint that subscribed to any other event type, or to all types via an empty list, receives nothing and gets no error.

title: a raising in-process subscriber prevents webhook enqueue for an already-committed event
what_is_wrong: `await subscriber(envelope)` runs unguarded before the webhook block, so one failing subscriber propagates out of `dispatch` after the event was committed and the webhook rows are never created.

title: naive datetime.utcnow() written into a timezone-aware column and compared against an aware value
what_is_wrong: `next_attempt_at=datetime.utcnow()` stores a naive timestamp while `_claim_batch` filters with `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, so the comparison mixes naive and aware datetimes and the stored instant is wrong by the UTC offset.

title: ORM rows are returned after their session has been closed
what_is_wrong: The rows are loaded inside `with session_scope()` and returned once the block exits, so every later attribute read in `deliver` (`delivery.attempts`, `delivery.payload`, `delivery.id`) touches a detached instance.

title: endpoint is loaded in a session that closes before it is used
what_is_wrong: `endpoint = session.get(...)` is the whole body of the `with` block, and `endpoint.signing_secret` / `endpoint.url` are then read in `send_once` outside any session.

title: missing None check on the endpoint lookup
what_is_wrong: If the endpoint row was deleted after the delivery was enqueued, `session.get` returns None and `send_once` dereferences `endpoint.signing_secret`, raising AttributeError instead of failing the delivery.

title: time.sleep() inside an async function blocks the event loop
what_is_wrong: The retry pause uses the blocking `time.sleep(delay)` rather than `asyncio.sleep`, so one retrying delivery freezes every other coroutine gathered in the same batch as well as the worker loop.

title: lock acquisition is a non-atomic GET followed by SET
what_is_wrong: Two workers that both observe an empty `LOCK_KEY` before either writes it will both return True, so the batch claim the lock is meant to serialize runs concurrently.

title: TTL is set in a separate command from the lock value
what_is_wrong: `set` and `expire` are two round trips, so a crash or connection drop between them leaves `webhooks:dispatch:lock` with no expiry and the worker pool permanently blocked.

title: the 60s lock TTL is shorter than a batch can take and release is unfenced
what_is_wrong: A single delivery can span five 30s-timeout attempts plus 30s of sleeps, so the lock expires mid-batch, another worker starts, and the `finally: redis_client.delete(LOCK_KEY)` then deletes the lock the second worker now holds.

title: gather without return_exceptions aborts the whole batch on one failure
what_is_wrong: The first delivery to raise anything propagates out of `gather`, so the remaining coroutines are abandoned mid-flight and their rows stay `in_flight`.

title: the worker loop has no exception handling and exits permanently on the first error
what_is_wrong: A Redis outage in `_acquire_lock`, a DB error in `_claim_batch`, or any exception escaping `gather` propagates out of `run_worker`, ending the only dispatch loop with no restart or backoff.

title: rows marked in_flight are never reset, so an interrupted delivery is never retried
what_is_wrong: `_claim_batch` flips status to `in_flight` and only `_finish` moves it out, so any crash, cancellation, or exception path leaves the row stuck in `in_flight`, which the pending filter never selects again.

title: retries are held in-process instead of rescheduled through next_attempt_at
what_is_wrong: The `while True` loop keeps the delivery in memory and writes `attempts` only once at `_finish`, so the persisted `next_attempt_at` schedule is never used and a process restart loses every attempt already made.

title: 4xx responses are retried like transient failures
what_is_wrong: Any status outside 200-299 falls through to the retry branch, so a 400 or 404 is re-POSTed up to MAX_ATTEMPTS instead of being marked permanent immediately.

title: follow_redirects=True re-sends the signed payload to a redirect target
what_is_wrong: The client follows 3xx responses, so a registered endpoint can answer with a Location header and have the signed body and signature delivered to an arbitrary host, including internal addresses.

title: the full header dict including the HMAC signature is logged at INFO
what_is_wrong: `log.info("POST %s headers=%s", endpoint.url, headers)` writes the per-request signature and timestamp headers into the application log on every attempt.

title: the remote response body is stored and logged in full with no truncation
what_is_wrong: `response_body = detail` persists the entire `response.text` into a TEXT column and the retry warning logs it too, so an endpoint controls unbounded log and row growth and whatever content it returns.

title: the request body carries no event envelope, so event_id is never transmitted
what_is_wrong: Only `delivery.payload` is posted, without `event_id` or `event_type`, so a receiver has nothing stable to deduplicate on.

title: the organizations.webhooks_enabled flag added by the migration is never consulted
what_is_wrong: The endpoint query filters on `org_id` and `active` only, so turning `webhooks_enabled` off for an organization has no effect on delivery.

title: missing None check on the delivery lookup
what_is_wrong: `row = session.get(m.WebhookDelivery, delivery_id)` is followed immediately by attribute assignment, so a deleted row raises AttributeError and the delivery result is lost.

title: the claim relies solely on a Redis lock with no row-level DB locking
what_is_wrong: The SELECT has no `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and no conditional UPDATE, so whenever the Redis lock fails open two workers select and send the same rows.

title: an entire batch of 100 deliveries is gathered with no concurrency limit
what_is_wrong: `asyncio.gather` over the whole `BATCH_SIZE` batch opens up to 100 simultaneous outbound requests from one client with no semaphore.

title: httpx.InvalidURL is not an HTTPError and escapes the retry loop
what_is_wrong: A malformed stored URL raises `httpx.InvalidURL`, which the `except httpx.HTTPError` does not catch, so the exception leaves `deliver` and takes the batch down with it.

title: backoff has no jitter and no ceiling
what_is_wrong: `BASE_DELAY_SECONDS**attempt` is fully deterministic, so all deliveries that failed in the same batch retry at exactly the same instants.

title: blocking synchronous DB work is performed inside async functions
what_is_wrong: `session_scope` and the SQLAlchemy queries are synchronous calls made from `async def` bodies, so each one stalls the event loop for the duration of the query.

title: to_dict returns the signing secret, which the listing endpoint exposes on every call
what_is_wrong: `"signing_secret": self.signing_secret` is part of the serialized form used by both create and `list_webhook_endpoints`, so the secret is readable at any time by anyone who can list endpoints.

title: timestamp columns are declared timezone-aware while the migration creates them without a time zone
what_is_wrong: `DateTime(timezone=True)` on `created_at`, `updated_at` and `next_attempt_at` does not match the migration's `TIMESTAMP`, so offsets are dropped on write and values come back naive.

title: the status vocabulary diverges from the migration's CHECK constraint
what_is_wrong: `STATUSES` lists `failed_permanent` while the migration allows `failed`, and the constant is never referenced anywhere so nothing detects the mismatch.

title: the timestamp columns omit nullable=False and updated_at has no onupdate
what_is_wrong: The migration declares both NOT NULL and the model does not, and `updated_at` is refreshed only by the manual assignment in `_finish`, so the status change in `_claim_batch` leaves it stale.

title: column length disagrees with the migration
what_is_wrong: The model declares `String(100)` where the migration creates unbounded `TEXT`, so the ORM will reject or truncate values the database accepts.

title: signing secrets are generated with the non-cryptographic random module
what_is_wrong: `random.choice` draws from the Mersenne Twister PRNG seeded from process state, so an attacker who observes any output can reconstruct the generator and predict other tenants' secrets.

title: the signed bytes are a re-serialization of the payload, not the bytes actually sent
what_is_wrong: `serialize` uses `json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True)` with default separators while the request body is encoded independently by httpx's `json=`, so the digest is computed over a different byte string than the receiver sees.

title: the timestamp is returned but never included in the MAC
what_is_wrong: The HMAC covers only the serialized payload, so `X-Acme-Timestamp` is unauthenticated and can be rewritten freely, which removes the replay protection the documented five-minute window depends on.

title: signature comparison uses == instead of a constant-time compare
what_is_wrong: `return expected == signature` short-circuits on the first differing character, leaking digest bytes through timing to anyone who can call verify repeatedly.

title: verify discards the timestamp and enforces no expiry
what_is_wrong: It re-signs with a fresh `int(time.time())` and ignores it, so a signature stays valid forever and no age check is possible through this API.

title: the constant is named for bytes but used as a character count
what_is_wrong: `range(SECRET_BYTES)` picks 32 characters from a 62-symbol alphabet, so the secret carries about 190 bits rather than the 256 the name implies.

title: a non-JSON-serializable payload raises TypeError from inside sign
what_is_wrong: `json.dumps` is called with no default handler, so a payload containing a datetime or Decimal raises out of `sign` and out of `send_once` rather than failing the delivery cleanly.

title: the documented scheme restriction is not what the route enforces
what_is_wrong: The code accepts anything whose scheme starts with "http", so `http://` endpoints are registered despite the documentation promising TLS only.

title: the documented signature formula does not match the code
what_is_wrong: The document says the HMAC covers `"{timestamp}.{raw_request_body}"`, while `sign` keys only over `json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True)`, so any receiver implementing the documentation rejects every delivery.

title: jitter is documented but not implemented
what_is_wrong: `backoff_for` returns exactly `2**attempt` seconds with no randomization.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "a 4xx is permanent and we stop immediately"
title: the documented 4xx handling contradicts the retry loop
what_is_wrong: `deliver` treats every non-2xx identically and retries a 4xx up to five times.

file: docs/webhooks.md — "it cannot be read back afterwards"
title: the documented secrecy of the signing secret is false
what_is_wrong: `GET /v1/settings/webhook-endpoints` serializes each endpoint with `to_dict()`, which includes `signing_secret`.

title: the documented org scoping of the deliveries endpoint does not exist
what_is_wrong: The document says the endpoint returns attempts "for an endpoint belonging to your organization", but `list_deliveries` filters on `endpoint_id` alone.

title: the deduplication key the document tells customers to use is never sent
what_is_wrong: Only the raw event payload is POSTed, with no `event_id` field or header, so a receiver has no way to follow this instruction.

title: the CHECK constraint rejects the status the code writes
what_is_wrong: The constraint allows `'failed'` while `_finish` writes `"failed_permanent"`, so every permanently failed delivery raises a constraint violation instead of being recorded.

title: the unique index on event_id alone prevents fan-out to more than one endpoint
what_is_wrong: `enqueue_for_event` inserts one row per matching endpoint with the same `event_id`, so the second row violates the unique index and the whole enqueue fails for any org with two endpoints.

title: timestamp columns are created without a time zone while the code uses aware datetimes
what_is_wrong: `created_at`, `updated_at` and `next_attempt_at` are `TIMESTAMP`, so the `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` values the code writes lose their offset and come back naive.

title: the signing secret is stored in plaintext
what_is_wrong: `signing_secret TEXT NOT NULL` keeps a live shared HMAC key in the clear, so a database dump or a SQL-level read hands over every tenant's key.

title: no composite index supports the claim query
what_is_wrong: The claim filters on `status` and `next_attempt_at` and orders by `next_attempt_at`, but only a single-column index on `status` exists, so the low-selectivity `pending` bucket must be sorted on every poll.

title: no index supports the deliveries listing query
what_is_wrong: `list_deliveries` filters on `endpoint_id` and orders by `created_at DESC`, and neither column is indexed.

title: the migration has no rollback and is not re-runnable
what_is_wrong: `CREATE TABLE` and `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` are unconditional with no `IF NOT EXISTS` and no down script, so a partially applied or repeated run fails.

title: the retry behaviour named in the commit subject is never exercised
what_is_wrong: Only `backoff_for`, `MAX_ATTEMPTS` and `send_once` are tested; `deliver`, `_claim_batch`, `_acquire_lock`, `_finish` and `enqueue_for_event` have no test, so the blocking sleep, the detached rows and the stuck `in_flight` state all pass CI.

title: the round-trip test cannot detect the documented-scheme mismatch
what_is_wrong: It signs and verifies with the same function, so it stays green whether or not the timestamp and the raw body are part of the MAC.

title: the test checks the signature's shape but never that it validates against the sent body
what_is_wrong: It asserts only that the header starts with `sha256=`, so the mismatch between `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True)` and the bytes httpx actually transmits is invisible.

title: the test asserts a constant against a literal and pins no behaviour
what_is_wrong: `assert MAX_ATTEMPTS == 5` can only fail if the constant is edited, and it says nothing about how many attempts `deliver` performs.

title: the test pins jitter-free delays that the documentation says should be jittered
what_is_wrong: Asserting exact equality with 2, 4, 8, 16 locks in the behaviour that contradicts `docs/webhooks.md`.

title: the test encodes the bytes-versus-characters confusion as the expected contract
what_is_wrong: It asserts `len(secret) == len(prefix) + SECRET_BYTES`, so a 32-character base62 secret is treated as correct and any move to 32 real random bytes would fail the test.

title: the fakes are class-attribute stubs that cannot reproduce the production object lifecycle
what_is_wrong: They always have populated `url`, `signing_secret` and `payload`, so the detached-instance and None-endpoint failures in `deliver` cannot surface through these tests.

title: no test asserts that a tampered payload fails verification
what_is_wrong: Both verify tests vary the secret, never the payload, so a signature computed over the wrong data would still be accepted by the suite.
